MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  FEBRUARY 12, 2019

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order by
MAYOR MITCHELL at 6:00 p.m. and the City Council convened into closed session in the City
Manager’s Office, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, California.

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None.

City Staff Present:  City Manager Douglas R. Prichard
  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer

CLOSED SESSION (TAKEN OUT OF ORDER)

A.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION
  Government Code Section 54957; Title: City Manager (Quarterly Evaluation)

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION

  ***

MAYOR MITCHELL adjourned the Closed Session portion of the meeting at 6:50 p.m.

At 7:00 p.m., MAYOR MITCHELL called the meeting back to order in open session in the City Council
Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, California.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

Members of Boy Scout Troop 276 led the Pledge of Allegiance.

ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  Assistant City Manager, Greg Grammer
  City Attorney, Donald M. Davis
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Planning Director David Wahba
  Community Services Director Andy Clark
  Assistant to the City Manager Alexa Davis
  Senior Planner Jeannie Naughton
  City Clerk Heidi Luce

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
FEBRUARY 12, 2019
 CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  CERTIFICATES OF RECOGNITION: “SPIRIT OF ACCESSIBILITY AWARD”

  MAYOR MITCHELL presented a Certificate of Recognition to Juanita Navarette and Martin
  Gombert from Palos Verdes Peninsula Transit Authority and Lori Dixon, PVPUSD Miraleste
  Intermediate School teacher commemorating their Spirit of Accessibility Award.

CONSENT CALENDAR

  The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the City Council.
  There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote.
  (Items removed for individual consideration will be voted on separately.)

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS A-G AS
  PRESENTED BELOW.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF JANUARY 22, 2019

  APPROVED AS PRESENTED.

C.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS – JANUARY AND FEBRUARY 2019

  APPROVED WARRANTS 61065 THROUGH 61117 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $269,566.34; AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 010119 THROUGH 010619;
  60935 THROUGH 60986; 60958 (Void); 60994 (Void); 61016 (Void); 61025
  THROUGH 61054; 61027 (Void); 61034 (Void-Printer Testing); 61036 (Void) IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $656,913.77 FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF $926,480.11 WITH
  PROPER AUDIT.

D.  SEARCH FOR NEW AUDIT/CPA FIRM UPDATE

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

E.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF JANUARY 28, 2019

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

F.  GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES OF JANUARY 29, 2019

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
FEBRUARY 12, 2019
 G.  PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 4, 2019

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

A.  SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA EDISON: Wildfire Mitigation, Safety and Grid Resiliency

Representatives from Southern California Edison provided an update on SCE current efforts related
to wildfire mitigation, safety and grid resiliency.

OTHER PUBLIC COMMENT:

Jake Ridout provided a legislative update from Assembly Member Al Muratsuchi’s office and provided
information on upcoming events in the area.

David Walbeck provided an update on the ongoing labor dispute between employees and management
of the Los Angeles County Sanitation Districts.

Angie Gilbride, Cal Water, provided an update on the status of the Palos Verdes Peninsula Water
Reliability Project.

PUBLIC HEARINGS (7:30 P.M.)

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 02-19: ORDINANCE NO. 724 AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY
  OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES AMENDING AND RESTATING CHAPTER 16.04 OF THE
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE PERTAINING TO SUBDIVISIONS AND
  REPEALING CHAPTERS 16.12, 16.16 AND 16.20 OF THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES
  MUNICIPAL CODE

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) open the Public Hearing; 2) take public testimony;
  3) discuss Ordinance No. 724; 4) close the Public Hearing; and 5) conduct second reading
  and adopt Ordinance No. 724

  Planning Director David Wahba provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING ON THIS MATTER.

  Hearing no objection, MAYOR MITCHELL so ordered.

  MAYOR MITCHELL called for public comment. Hearing none, she closed the publc hearing
  and called for comments from the City Council

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
FEBRUARY 12, 2019
   COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL ADOPT ORDINANCE NO. 724 AN ORDINANCE OF THE
  CITY OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES AMENDING AND RESTATING CHAPTER 16.04
  OF THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE PERTAINING TO
  SUBDIVISIONS AND REPEALING CHAPTERS 16.12, 16.16 AND 16.20 OF THE
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

  Prior to the roll call vote, City Clerk Luce read the ordinance by title.

B.  RESOLUTION NO. 2432 APPROVING THE PROPOSED USE OF 2019-20 COMMUNITY
  DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT (CDBG) FUNDS

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) open the Public Hearing; 2) receive any public
  testimony; 3) close the Public Hearing; and 4) waive further reading and approve Resolution
  No. 2432 authorizing the execution of a contract with the Los Angeles County Community
  Development Commission for participation in the program for funding of the ADA Access
  Ramp and Sidewalk Improvement Program as identified in the Programs and Conditions
  Assessment Report dated April 2, 2014 in the amount of approximately $23,514.

  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF regarding the timing of the sidewalk improvement
  program, Assistant City Manager Grammer explained that the program is a 14 year program
  with specific streets identified each year.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING ON THIS MATTER.

  Hearing no objection, MAYOR MITCHELL so ordered.

  MAYOR MITCHELL called for public comment.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING ON THIS MATTER.

  Hearing no objection, MAYOR MITCHELL so ordered and called for comments from the City
  Council

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
FEBRUARY 12, 2019
   COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2432 AUTHORIZING THE
  EXECUTION OF A CONTRACT WITH THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY COMMUNITY
  DEVELOPMENT COMMISSION FOR PARTICIPATION IN THE PROGRAM FOR
  FUNDING OF THE ADA ACCESS RAMP AND SIDEWALK IMPROVEMENT
  PROGRAM AS IDENTIFIED IN THE PROGRAMS AND CONDITIONS
  ASSESSMENT REPORT DATED APRIL 2, 2014 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  APPROXIMATELY $23,514.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

Prior to the roll call vote, City Clerk Luce read the resolution by title.

NEW BUSINESS

A.  MASTER AGREEMENT WITH WILLDAN ENGINEERING AND PROPOSAL FOR
  PROFESSIONAL ENGINEERING SERVICES FOR 2019 STREET RESURFACING PROJECT

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) approve the Master Professional Services
  Agreement with Willdan Engineering dated February 12, 2109 and 2) approve the Proposal
  from Willdan Engineering to provide professional engineering services for design,
  construction management and observation services for the 2019 Street Resurfacing Project
  in a not-to-exceed amount of $139,210 (including $22,800 for the City of Rolling Hills portion.)

  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN regarding validation of the quotes provided
  by Willdan, Assistant City Manager Grammer explained that the costs for Willdan’s services
  are compared as a percentage of the total construction cost for the project with 10-15% being
  the estimated threshold depending on the specific services provided. He noted that the City
  recently went out to bid for these services and Willdan was competitively priced; and because
  of the years that Willdan has provided services to the City, they have a familiarity with the
  City.

  City Attorney Davis commented that services provided in an amount over the City Manager’s
  $25,000 threshold for signature will be brought before the Council for review.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE THE MASTER PROFESSIONAL SERVICES
  AGREEMENT WITH WILLDAN ENGINEERING DATED FEBRUARY 12, 2019 AND
  2) APPROVE THE PROPOSAL FROM WILLDAN ENGINEERING TO PROVIDE
  PROFESSIONAL ENGINEERING SERVICES FOR DESIGN, CONSTRUCTION
  MANAGEMENT AND OBSERVATION SERVICES FOR THE 2019 STREET
  RESURFACING PROJECT IN A NOT-TO-EXCEED AMOUNT OF $139,210
  (INCLUDING $22,800 FOR THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS PORTION.)

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
FEBRUARY 12, 2019
 B.  AUTHORIZATION TO AWARD CONTRACT FOR THE CITY HALL RENOVATION PROJECT
  AND TO PURCHASE RELATED EQUIPMENT AND FURNITURE

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) reject the bid protest letter filed by Concept
  Consultant, Inc. and award a contract to PUB Construction, Inc. for the City Hall Renovation
  Project in the amount of $383,550, plus a 10% contingency of $38,355 for a total amount of
  $421,905; and 2) authorize staff to purchase office equipment in the amount of $80,000;
  purchase audio visual equipment in the amount of $13,000; rent office trailers and furniture
  in the amount of $25,000; and, provide for contract administration and management services
  in the amount of $30,000.

  Planning Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF regarding the office equipment and the audio
  visual equipment, Administrative Services Director Whitehead explained that the full cost
  includes new office furniture to replace the current dilapidated furniture and audio visual
  equipment for the new conference room.

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN regarding the mistake made on the bid,
  Planning Director Wahba confirmed that staff has reviewed all other aspects of the bid and is
  comfortable proceeding.

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN regarding other projects done by this
  company, Planning Director Wahba noted that the reference list is included in the bid
  documents and the references have been checked.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL 1) REJECT THE BID PROTEST LETTER FILED BY
  CONCEPT CONSULTANT, INC. AND AWARD A CONTRACT TO PUB
  CONSTRUCTION, INC. FOR THE CITY HALL RENOVATION PROJECT IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $383,550, PLUS A 10% CONTINGENCY OF $38,355 FOR A TOTAL
  OF $421,905; AND 2) AUTHORIZED STAFF TO PURCHASE OFFICE EQUIPMENT
  IN THE AMOUNT OF $80,000; PURCHASE AUDIO VISUAL EQUIPMENT IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $13,000; RENT OFFICE TRAILERS AND FURNITURE IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $25,000; AND PROVIDE FOR CONTRACT ADMINISTRATION AND
  MANAGEMENT SERVICES IN THE AMOUNT OF $30,000.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

OLD BUSINESS

At COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN’S suggestion recognizing that the representatives from Cal
Water are present, MAYOR MITCHELL took Old Business Item C out of order.

C.  CAL WATER 2018 GENERAL RATE CASE COMMENT LETTER

  Recommendation: That the City Council review the draft comment letter and provide direction
  for additional comments. Staff will attend the Public Participation Hearing and continue to
  update the City Council as new information becomes available.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
FEBRUARY 12, 2019
   Senior Planner Jeannie Naughton provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)

  Greg Milleman, Vice President, California Rates provided an overview of the CPUC process
  for approving rate increases related to infrastructure improvement projects. He stated that the
  total project cost is $96 million which results in a rate increase of approximately $1/day per
  customer.

  Carmelo Sorce provided an overview of the items that account for the cost increase for the
  project between 2015 and 2018 and the overall timeline for the project.

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN regarding the costs passed on to each of
  the 24,000 customers, Mr. Milleman explained that the rate per customer varies based on
  several factor. He further explained the portion of costs that are borne by the shareholders.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN thanked Cal Water for taking the time to meet with him and
  staff to explain the costs associated with the project and that he looks forward to continuing
  to work collaboratively on this matter for the benefit of the ratepayers. He suggested that he
  and MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ be assigned to a subcommittee to further address this
  matter.

  In response to MAYOR MITCHELL, Mr. Sorce explained that they have included a
  contingency for unexpected expenses in the amount submitted and they don’t anticipate any
  additional expenses; but given the complexity of the project, it is possible that unforeseen
  expenses may arise.

  Following discussion, COUNCIL concurred on the following action:

  1) DIRECT STAFF TO FINALIZE THE COMMENT LETTER AND SUBMIT IT TO THE
  CPUC AND THAT THE CITY COUNCIL; AND 2) MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ AND
  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN TO SERVE AS AN AD HOC COMMITTEE TO
  ADDRESS THIS MATTER.
